title: The stack, arranged by where it runs
caption: Interface, services, models, data, and the machines underneath. Read left to right: a request enters at the interface and the cost of answering it goes up with every column.

nodes.label: Next.js 16
nodes.role: App Router on every front end I have shipped. Server components mean the data-shaping code sits next to the query instead of in a client bundle.

nodes.label: TypeScript
nodes.role: Strict mode, no implicit any. The project data on this site is typed at the source, so a case study that references a project that does not exist fails the build rather than the page.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS
nodes.role: Every colour on this site is a token in one config file. That is the only reason the dark-to-light rewrite was a config change instead of a fourteen-file edit.

nodes.label: Three.js
nodes.role: One Points cloud, one draw call, a custom vertex shader injected through onBeforeCompile. Used where 6,236 objects have to move at 60fps on a phone, and nowhere else.

nodes.label: Recharts
nodes.role: Dashboard charting where the numbers change. Static figures are rendered in matplotlib at analysis time instead, because a chart that never changes should not cost a chart library.

nodes.label: FastAPI
nodes.role: The Python side of every split app. Where the model lives, because moving a PyTorch checkpoint into a Node process is a worse problem than one HTTP hop.

nodes.label: Route handlers
nodes.role: Next.js server routes for anything that does not need Python. On this site they are all force-static so the same code can build for a server or for a bucket.

nodes.label: NextAuth v5
nodes.role: Session and role handling. In FORGE the mentor and learner roles are what gate week release, so auth is business logic, not a login form.

nodes.label: Prisma 7
nodes.role: Schema-first, migrations in the repo. The schema is the document I reach for when I come back to a project after two months.

nodes.label: PyTorch
nodes.role: CTGAN implemented from the 2019 paper rather than imported: mode-specific normalisation, a PacGAN critic, WGAN-GP, conditional training-by-sampling. CPU only, because there is no GPU here.

nodes.label: scikit-learn
nodes.role: Logistic regression where a scorecard has to be explained to a credit committee, and the train-on-synthetic-test-on-real classifier that scores NOVA output.

nodes.label: PyMC
nodes.role: Bayesian Poisson Lee-Carter with NUTS. Fixing the intercept at the empirical mean and putting b on a simplex is what finally made the chains mix.

nodes.label: sentence-transformers
nodes.role: Embeddings for retrieval and for the verse cloud. Run once at build time and shipped as vectors, which is why neither project pays for an inference server.

nodes.label: lifelines
nodes.role: Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards for the life book. Concordance 0.77, reported on held-out policies.

nodes.label: transformers.js
nodes.role: The query embedding runs in the visitor browser. No inference endpoint means no bill and no cold start, and it is the reason AYAT costs nothing to keep online.

nodes.label: Hosted LLM APIs
nodes.role: Open weights on NVIDIA NIM, with a second provider behind them. Every call site assumes the model id can retire, because one already did.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.role: The default. Relational until something proves it should not be.

nodes.label: Supabase
nodes.role: Managed Postgres plus auth for HireIQ. Also the reason HireIQ is currently down at the data layer, which is its own lesson about depending on a free project that can be reclaimed.

nodes.label: Vector store
nodes.role: Section-level chunks of thirteen Acts. Small enough that the honest engineering answer was a plain index, not a hosted vector database.

nodes.label: pandas and NumPy
nodes.role: Every pipeline that starts at a public API and ends at a model.

nodes.label: Generated artefacts
nodes.role: Forecasts, coordinates and diagrams computed once at build time and committed. A generated file you can read in a diff is a generated file somebody checks.

nodes.label: Docker
nodes.role: Multi-stage builds, CPU-only wheels, standalone output. Getting the NOVA image from 2.5 GB to 367 MB was a day of work and the difference between deployable and not.

nodes.label: Coolify
nodes.role: Open-source platform-as-a-service on my own droplet. Git push, it rebuilds, it swaps the container.

nodes.label: DigitalOcean droplet
nodes.role: One small Ubuntu box. The point is not that it is better than Vercel, it is that I know what is on it.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions
nodes.role: Builds the static fallback of this site and pushes it to Pages, so there is always a free copy online.

nodes.label: Vercel
nodes.role: Where most of these projects still live. Free, fast, and the reason the infrastructure question was easy to postpone.

nodes.label: Uptime Kuma
nodes.role: Self-hosted monitoring. If I am going to claim uptime on a portfolio, something other than me has to be measuring it.
